transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~28 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (NexaHealth Head of ML), Mark Davis (Nexa DevOps), Tessa Nguyen (Product)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll keep this to 30 - 30 minutes ish. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Priya: Priya here.
[00:12] Mark: Mark on my side.
[00:14] Tessa: Tessa here.
[00:16] Daniel: Daniel from Redwood.
[00:18] Alex: Cool. Agenda - onboarding progress, staging access, security questions, and then the benchmark plan. Any additions?
[00:25] Priya: Sounds good. We mostly just want to confirm timeline and make sure you can run the latency tests we discussed.
[00:30] Alex: Perfect. Quick update from our side: we uploaded the SOC2 excerpts and the security pack to the shared folder yesterday - link in the deck - and Daniel's got a short benchmark script ready.
[00:42] Daniel: Yeah I'll walk through the plan after we confirm access. The script does a warmup sequence, then runs variable seq lengths, measures p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec. It also toggles batching sizes.
[00:55] Mark: Right - on our side we ran into a snag with the peering for the staging VPC last week, so it's not yet provisioned. I expect that to be done by middle of next week. I can, though, create a short-lived jump host or run the test from a VM if needed.
[01:10] Alex: Ok that helps. The ideal is VPC peering so the traffic path matches prod, but a jump host will work for initial runs. We need: pem/key for the test VM, security group rules to allow outbound to Redwood endpoints, and an example payload size.
[01:25] Mark: I'll add the SG rules, and can share a test user/ssh key. Do you need SAML SSO tokens or just the service creds?
[01:32] Daniel: For the benchmark the service creds are easiest. For the private deployment review later we'll need SAML details.
[01:38] Tessa: On the product side we're tracking success criteria - 100ms p95 for small prompts, under 300ms for medium, and consistent throughput for batching. Priya's team will provide the prompt set.
[01:49] Priya: Yep, I'll export a representative prompt set today. Note some prompts are multi-turn and require KV cache behavior to be preserved.
[01:55] Alex: Good call - KV cache is important. Quick question for Daniel: when you run with KV caching, do you simulate cache hit rates?
[02:03] Daniel: We can. The script supports a few modes: cold-starts, warm cache, and synthetic hit rates. We'll run both cold and warm to show delta. Expect 20-30% latency improvement on warm runs depending on sequence. That also changes batching recommendations.
[02:21] Mark: Re: encryption - we need to confirm KMS integration. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys/HSM?
[02:29] Alex: Yes, we support KMS/Multi-tenant HSM options for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we have envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS for certain contracts. I'll attach the KMS section in the security pack.
[02:42] Priya: Can you share whether audit logs include token-level events? Our compliance folks asked.
[02:48] Daniel: Audit logs capture request metadata, model version, route, timestamps, and we can include request IDs and user IDs. We don't log full prompt text by default unless configured - we have redaction and retention policies.
[02:58] Priya: Ok that's helpful. We'll need configurable retention and ability to pull logs for audits.
[03:05] Alex: Noted. We'll include retention options in the packet.
[03:10] Tessa: About model variants - we were wondering if you can fallback to a cheaper quantized variant automatically when capacity is constrained.
[03:18] Daniel: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible variants; we can set policy by latency SLO or cost target. The tradeoff is potential quality regression, so we usually recommend A/Bing those.
[03:32] Priya: Speaking of regression, do you have eval hooks to detect output quality drift?
[03:36] Alex: Redwood Optimize ties evaluation sets to alerts; we can run batch evals and set regression thresholds against your gold prompts. We'll propose a baseline in the next deck.
[03:45] Mark: Back to the access stuff - timeline: I can provision a test VM and creds by Monday 2027-01-18. Is that late for the benchmark?
[03:55] Daniel: That's fine; we'd like to do the benchmark on 2027-01-19 then. I'll block an hour and share the run instructions.
[04:03] Alex: Great. I'll also send the pilot pricing worksheet with recommended batching configs - that will show cost/latency tradeoffs for different qprofiles.
[04:10] Priya: On quantization: do you have recommended profiles for our Llama-ish model family? We've seen mixed results with 4-bit.
[04:18] Daniel: We have verified profiles for several open families; for Llama variants we usually recommend 4-bit quant with per-channel calibration for best perf/quality tradeoff. We'll include specific numbers after we see your evaluation set.
[04:30] Tessa: Any blockers on your side?
[04:32] Alex: No blockers. We just need access, sample prompts, and confirmation on which model variant to benchmark.
[04:40] Priya: We'll default to the Llama-2 13B equivalently configured variant for now - we'll share exact model name in the prompt set.
[04:49] Mark: One quick infra note: our staging has strict egress controls; I may need to coordinate with networking to open the specific IP ranges. Can you provide a minimal IP list?
[04:59] Alex: Yes - we'll send a minimal egress IP list. Also provide your preferred connection pattern, e.g., outbound HTTPS to endpoint or direct TCP peer.
[05:10] Mark: Outbound HTTPS is preferred.
[05:13] Daniel: For the latency numbers it's fine. If you want lower network hop variability we can run from a VM inside the peered VPC later.
[05:21] Priya: For retention and PII masking, can you confirm default retention and options?
[05:27] Alex: Default retention is 30 days for request metadata; prompt retention is 90 days if enabled. We can customize per contract. We'll include the options in the security docs.
[05:38] Tessa: Great. Anything else - pricing?
[05:41] Alex: Pilot pricing worksheet will be in the follow-up. It shows dedicated reserved nodes vs hosted pay-as-you-go and expected token-based cost at the sample workload.
[05:52] Priya: One more question: does Redwood support role-based access and SSO SCIM provisioning?
[05:58] Daniel: Yes, RBAC and SCIM provisioning for user sync are supported. For enterprise we can set up SAML SSO and SCIM.
[06:06] Mark: OK.
[06:08] Alex: Cool. To recap - action items: Alex will send security pack + IP list + pilot pricing by Friday 2027-01-15, Daniel will prepare benchmark script and instructions, Mark will provision test creds by 2027-01-18, Priya will send prompts by 2027-01-15. Benchmark scheduled 2027-01-19.
[06:23] Tessa: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:26] Priya: Thanks.
[06:28] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the links.

Notes / artifacts referenced:
- Security pack (link): https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/nexahealth
- Benchmark script (placeholder): will be shared in the run instructions doc
- Pilot pricing worksheet: link will be shared in follow-up email

End of transcript.
